My dad recently showed me The Gentleman which was my first introduction to Guy Ritchie and I gotta say I really didn’t like it.  I’ve only seen two of this guy’s films so far and to be honest I don’t think I’m keen on the style of movies he makes. That being said, and while I definitely didn't love this one either, this movie does has enough charm and wit for me to enjoy it for the most part.

This movie has a special place in my heart, I've seen it multiple times. Parts of it are icky, other parts are funny, others are entertaining. The editing, music cues, and sound editing are fantastic and a lot of the rest becomes baffling with the hindsight of 20 years. It is fascinating to consider that Guy Ritchie keeps chugging along as a filmmaker, but an argument can be made that their peak was this movie. [I feel most people would argue for the Sherlock Holmes movies.] When and how did Guy Ritchie loose the spark that's in this movie?

The British are not cool, whether they’re black or white. Never thought much of Russians or Jews either. The best parts of this movie are when Mickey’s around. Wished it was a little more focused on him, and was just a singular narrative instead of being British Pulp Fiction. And man, the editing. Quite a product of its time! They go hard on digital zooms for some reason and it looks like crap. “Woahhh cool things happening, play some fast music and just digital zoom in and out!” Moronic. A lot of other editing choices are quite good. I like the montage of the American leaving/coming to London. I really like when Mickey goes underwater during that last boxing match. Some editing decisions just made the events confusing. Why does Tony and the American just let Boris walk away? Do they assume he’s dead? I mean, I sure did. Why don’t the black guys kill him? Do they ALSO assume he’s dead? Man the black guys are honestly just totally stupid. Not locking doors, pulling a gun on Tony and then just walking away…not sure why theyre just dumped on again and again. And when that British guy walks in on then with the dead body, they just stand around and let him monologue? And then they just follow him around? What are you guys DOING . Are you stupid? I think it’s just bad writing honestly. “Crime doesnt pay”, so in order to continually punish the characters the script just makes them stupid. Also the poster is really quite colorful for such a drab movie. Pick a lane…
